title: Pardons William E. Henry
description_medium: President Donald Trump granted William E. Henry a full pardon on January 19, 2021. DOJ lists a Middle District of Alabama theft-of-government-property conviction, for which Henry received two years of probation and a $4,000 fine in May 2019. The pardon warrant confirms that it was full and unconditional.
blockers: The DOJ clemency entry identifies the offense and sentence but gives no account of the property or underlying conduct.
rationale: The available record supports the stated event but lacks this case-specific detail.

title: Pardons Kenneth Kurson in Federal Cyberstalking Case
description_medium: President Donald Trump pardoned Kenneth Kurson on January 19, 2021, before trial on federal cyberstalking and harassment charges. Prosecutors accused the former New York Observer editor of targeting three people, including his former wife. Kurson was a friend of Jared Kushner, who had owned the newspaper, and denied wrongdoing.
description_long: President Donald Trump pardoned Kenneth Kurson on January 19, 2021, before he could stand trial on federal cyberstalking and harassment charges. Prosecutors accused Kurson, a former editor of the New York Observer, of targeting three people, including his former wife, with threatening messages, anonymous calls and negative online reviews. Kurson denied wrongdoing. He was a friend of Jared Kushner, who had owned the Observer and appointed Kurson its editor. In August 2021, Manhattan prosecutors brought separate state charges accusing Kurson of accessing his former wife’s computer. Those later state allegations were not resolved by the federal pardon. The federal pardon applied to the listed federal charges; it did not dispose of any separate state prosecution. The DOJ list records no sentence for the federal case, consistent with the fact that the pardon came before trial.
rationale: Federal charges were unresolved at the time of the pardon; later state allegations concerned separate charges.

title: Pardons Brian Lyle McSwain
description_medium: President Donald Trump granted Brian Lyle McSwain a full pardon on January 19, 2021. McSwain had an 18-month federal sentence for a South Carolina conspiracy to distribute marijuana and cocaine. The White House said he had completed the sentence and cited his lost promotion opportunities because of the felony conviction; Senator Lindsey Graham and former prosecutors supported the pardon.
description_long: President Donald Trump granted Brian Lyle McSwain a full pardon on January 19, 2021. McSwain’s South Carolina federal conviction involved a conspiracy to distribute marijuana and cocaine. The Justice Department lists an 18-month prison term, followed by three years of supervised release, and a sentence amendment in 1994. The White House said McSwain had completed his prison term and had been passed over for promotions because of his felony conviction. It also said the pardon was supported by Senator Lindsey Graham, two former U.S. attorneys for South Carolina and other former law-enforcement officers. Those are the publicly stated grounds and supporters; the clemency records do not establish a personal relationship or improper exchange. The pardon removed federal consequences associated with the covered conviction, while the clemency release did not alter the historical sentence recorded in DOJ’s case summary. The warrant records the pardon as unconditional.
rationale: DOJ lists the conviction and sentence; White House statement provides the publicly stated grounds and supporters.

title: Pardons Glen Moss
description_medium: President Donald Trump granted Glen Moss a full pardon on January 19, 2021. DOJ associates him with a Connecticut case involving payment to an unlicensed physician and attempted tax evasion, and a South Carolina mail-fraud case. The list records probation, home confinement, a fine and restitution, but does not clarify which case the pardon covered.
blockers: The DOJ list associates Moss with two cases but does not establish whether the pardon covered both.
rationale: The available record supports the stated event but lacks this case-specific detail.

title: Pardons Eric Wesley Patton
description_medium: President Donald Trump granted Eric Wesley Patton a full pardon on January 19, 2021. DOJ identifies an Eastern District of Tennessee false-statement conviction and a $1,000 fine imposed in 1999. The pardon warrant names Patton and specifies the conviction covered, but does not describe the statement or give a recipient-specific reason for the grant.
description_long: The January 19, 2021 clemency warrant granted Eric Wesley Patton a full and unconditional pardon for his federal conviction in the Eastern District of Tennessee. The case charged a violation of the federal false-statement statute, and Patton was sentenced in February 1999 to a $1,000 fine and a $100 special assessment. The DOJ list independently identifies the conviction as making a false statement. The warrant confirms the action’s scope but does not describe the statement itself or explain why Patton was selected for clemency. It groups his name with several other recipients in the same instrument. The official records therefore establish the pardon, offense category and penalty, while leaving the underlying conduct and rationale unstated. The warrant was issued on the final day of Trump’s term and granted relief only for the conviction it names. No further case narrative appears in the warrant.
rationale: The warrant identifies the offense and penalty but does not describe the statement or give an individual rationale.
